cohort: Birthing people and newborns in three public hospital networks in Mexico
finding: The AMBAR midwifery-based training program for health care providers increased the use of beneficial birth practices, such as skin-to-skin contact and delayed cord clamping, and decreased the use of potentially harmful practices when overused, such as vaginal examinations and cesarean births.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth rates decreased significantly after the implementation of the AMBAR training program (P < 0.001).
